I am 60 years old and have farmed my whole life in Quzhou County. I never went to school, but I know this land well. My family has about 8 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. Every year I grow the same rotation as my neighbors — winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what this soil and climate are made for. I already sowed my wheat last October before the frost came, and now in early spring the wheat is greening up. I will manage it through to harvest in June, then immediately plant maize in the same fields. I do not experiment with new crops because I cannot afford to lose my family's food and income.

For my wheat, I use improved varieties like the ones from the county seed station — they yield better and resist lodging. I rotary till the land before sowing. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, and I topdress with urea when the wheat joints in spring. Water is precious, so I irrigate from my well about four times: the winter irrigation, one at green-up, one at jointing, and one at grain-filling. I spray for insects twice, spray herbicide once to control weeds, and use fungicide if I see disease after rainy spells. I expect about 1000 jin of wheat per mu if the weather cooperates.

For the summer maize, I plant hybrid seed — Denghai 605 or something similar from the shop — right after the wheat comes out in June. I do not till again; I plant no-till to save time and fuel because the rainy season is coming and I must get the seed in quickly. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing, and irrigate twice during the summer if the rains are not enough. I spray for insects two or three times and use herbicide once. I expect about 1100 jin per mu.

This double-cropping system feeds my family and gives me grain to sell. I have done it for decades and I trust it.
